items.title: Andrew Bailey Interview, 1959-09-30
items.q: Well I heard it when Louis Armstrong came on the record.

ctx.x: When did you first hear when the Saints go marching in? Did they ever sing that years ago?

No, no. Well I heard it when Louis Armstrong came on the record. Yeah. That's when Louis Armstrong come on the record. They go marching in. You never heard the band play at them before? No, not before Louis Armstrong. Sure didn't. And you didn't hear it in the church? No. Well they used to sing. Used to sing, but I know music. They used to sing. I know music.
Well that looks like about the end of the tape.

items.title: Andrew Bailey Interview, 1959-09-26
items.q: Caught me four and a half to see Louis Armstrong

ctx.x: Like Bates, could that be it?

He's from over the river, they say, but he's up north now. He with them. Yeah, I went to all of them when they came here, man. Caught me four and a half to see Louis Armstrong, and four and a nine, eight, twice. I ain't gonna pay no more. Yeah, they was at the auditorium, Louis Armstrong, I see, Lionel Hampton. It was a packed house, but I tell you, they went there most for that little son to come there, but his son didn't shoot up, Lionel Hampton. I seen Night King Cole.
Well, I just forgot to ask, I started to ask, did you ever know Ann Cook uptown?
